hero.description: The US-Iran conflict is spreading into another critical maritime corridor after Iran-aligned Houthi forces seized Yemen's strategic Mokha port, sending Brent crude sharply higher and increasing fears of a prolonged global energy shock.

featured.title: Oil Surges as Mokha Port Falls to Houthi Forces
featured.content: Global energy markets came under renewed pressure on Thursday after Iran-aligned Houthi forces seized the strategic Yemeni port of Mokha near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The development adds another major shipping risk to the existing disruption around the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude surged above $105 a barrel and briefly moved towards $107 as traders assessed the possibility of wider disruption to oil and commercial shipping routes. The Bab el-Mandeb is a major international trade corridor linking the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.
featured.imageQuery: Mokha Yemen port Bab el Mandeb Red Sea

articles.title: Brent Crude Surges Above $105
articles.content: Oil prices jumped sharply on Thursday as the seizure of Mokha by Iran-aligned Houthi forces raised fears that the energy crisis could spread beyond the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude rose above $105 and reached around $106–107 a barrel, its highest level since May. U.S. crude also moved above $100.
articles.imageQuery: Brent crude oil barrels price surge

articles.title: Houthis Seize Strategic Mokha Port in Yemen
articles.content: Iran-aligned Houthi forces have seized control of Mokha, a strategically important port on Yemen's Red Sea coast. The port lies close to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, one of the world's most important maritime chokepoints. The takeover represents a major escalation in Yemen's conflict and creates additional uncertainty for international shipping.
articles.imageQuery: Mokha Mocha Yemen port Red Sea

articles.title: Bab el-Mandeb Becomes New Focus of Global Shipping Risk
articles.content: The Bab el-Mandeb connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and is an important route for global trade. Instability around the passage could force more ships to take longer routes around Africa, increasing fuel, insurance and transportation costs. Shipping through the corridor has already fallen significantly since Houthi attacks began disrupting the route.
articles.imageQuery: Bab el Mandeb shipping route map

articles.title: US-Iran Conflict Continues to Drive Energy Market Fears
articles.content: The continuing confrontation between Washington and Tehran is increasingly affecting global energy markets. The latest escalation around Gulf and Red Sea shipping routes has raised concerns that disruptions could persist well beyond the immediate conflict.
articles.imageQuery: US Iran Middle East conflict oil shipping

articles.title: Dangote Secures 16 Million Barrels of Nigerian Crude for October
articles.content: Dangote Refinery has secured at least 16 million barrels of Nigerian crude for October delivery, according to industry sources cited by Reuters. The purchases amount to approximately 520,000 barrels per day and represent a substantial portion of the refinery's 700,000-barrel-per-day capacity. The refinery is increasing domestic crude intake as it prepares for its planned IPO.

articles.title: Dangote's Domestic Crude Purchases Increase
articles.content: The October purchases include Nigerian crude supplied through NNPC allocations as well as additional cargoes obtained through tenders. The refinery also secured U.S. WTI Midland cargoes. Kpler data showed Dangote received about 565,000 barrels per day of Nigerian crude in August, nearly twice its average intake from the previous year.
articles.imageQuery: Dangote refinery Lagos oil storage tanks

articles.title: Dangote-NMDPRA Legal Dispute Continues
articles.content: A Federal High Court in Lagos has extended an interim order restraining the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority from interfering with Dangote Refinery's operations while the legal dispute continues. The dispute centres on regulatory action involving propane loading and truck-out activities. The court has not yet determined the substantive issues.
articles.imageQuery: Federal High Court Lagos Nigeria courthouse

articles.title: Court Sends Dangote Regulatory Case Towards Reassignment
articles.content: Justice Akintayo Aluko said he could not set a substantive hearing date because his jurisdiction as a vacation judge was ending. The case file is therefore being returned to the registry for assignment to a regular court. The interim protection remains in force pending further proceedings.

articles.title: Kano Political Commentator Ibrahim Dan Shagamu Found Dead
articles.content: Ibrahim Khalil Dan Shagamu, a Kano-based social media political commentator known for outspoken views, was found dead at his residence in Gaida, Kumbotso Local Government Area. Family members and rights groups have called for a thorough investigation. Kano authorities have directed security agencies to investigate the circumstances and identify those responsible.

articles.title: Dan Shagamu Killing Raises Concerns Ahead of 2027 Elections
articles.content: The killing of Dan Shagamu has renewed concerns about the safety of political commentators and opposition voices as Nigeria moves towards the 2027 election cycle. Amnesty International has condemned the killing and called for those responsible to be brought to justice. The motive and circumstances remain under investigation.

articles.title: ECB Raises Interest Rate to 2.50%
articles.content: The European Central Bank has raised its key interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 2.50% as policymakers assess renewed inflation risks linked to higher energy prices. The Middle East conflict has complicated the outlook because prolonged increases in oil and gas prices could feed into transport, production and household costs.

articles.title: UK Government Borrowing Costs Hit Multi-Year Highs
articles.content: The UK's 10-year gilt yield climbed 10 basis points to 5.378% on Thursday, its highest level since July 2007. Longer-dated 20-year and 30-year yields also rose to levels not seen since 1998. Higher borrowing costs could place additional pressure on government finances ahead of the autumn budget.
articles.imageQuery: UK government bonds London financial markets

articles.title: Ukraine Faces Another Difficult Winter
articles.content: Ukraine is preparing for another challenging winter as Russian attacks continue to threaten energy, transport and other critical infrastructure. Concerns remain focused on air-defence capacity and the ability to protect essential services during another period of heavy winter demand.

articles.title: Philippines Ferry Fire Leaves Five Dead and 87 Missing
articles.content: At least five people have died and 87 remain unaccounted for after the M/V June Aster caught fire off Coron in Palawan. The ferry's manifest listed 134 people aboard. Forty-two people have been rescued so far, while search-and-rescue operations continue. Authorities stress that the figures may change as the operation progresses.

articles.title: Global Markets Under Pressure as Oil Surges
articles.content: Financial markets remain nervous as oil prices rise sharply and government bond yields climb. Investors are increasingly concerned that a prolonged energy shock could keep inflation elevated, complicating decisions by central banks and increasing borrowing costs for governments and businesses.
articles.imageQuery: global financial markets oil trading screens

articles.title: Critical Infrastructure Resilience Becomes a Global Concern
articles.content: The widening energy and geopolitical crisis is increasing attention on the resilience of critical infrastructure, including ports, energy networks, transport systems and digital services. Prolonged disruption to physical supply chains can also increase costs for technology and industrial businesses.

morningSummary.title: 🌍 RadiantWaves Evening News & Update
morningSummary.content: Good evening. The global energy crisis has intensified as Brent crude surged above $105 following the Houthi seizure of Yemen's strategic Mokha port near the Bab el-Mandeb. In Nigeria, Dangote Refinery has secured major October crude supplies while its regulatory dispute with NMDPRA continues in court. The killing of Kano political commentator Ibrahim Khalil Dan Shagamu has raised fresh security concerns, while Europe faces higher borrowing costs and renewed inflation pressure. In Asia, a ferry disaster in the Philippines has left five dead and dozens missing.

bigQuestion: As conflicts begin to affect oil, food, transport and household costs around the world, how prepared are governments and ordinary people for a prolonged period of global economic uncertainty?
